answer: The anchor test I would run is Attested florist association membership with florists association attestation: a membership the association kept across years of shops, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the karst compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The ivory grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
